The web platform moves more slowly than daily AI news suggests. Below are the three most relevant recent developments that *do* have a practical effect on this type of site right now, with precise names/dates where available. ### 2. Chrome 130 (released 1 October 2024) + updated CSP best-practice guidance
Chrome 130 shipped stricter default handling for cross-origin resource sharing and de-emphasised certain legacy security headers. More importantly, Google and Cloudflare updated their recommended CSP baseline in late September/early October 2024.

**Relevant deprecation/best-practice shift**:
- `X-XSS-Protection` and `X-Content-Type-Options` are now considered legacy/no-op in modern Chromium.
- Recommended replacement is a strict-but-usable CSP delivered via Cloudflare Pages `_headers`:
  ```
  Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-abc123' https://static.cloudflareinsights.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https://*.google-analytics.com; connect-src 'self' https://*.google-analytics.com https://plausible.io;
  ```
- Also requires `Permissions-Policy: interest-cohort=()` (FLoC/Topics API opt-out) and `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` for isolation.

For a static local-business site this reduces attack surface (especially important if you embed any third-party review widgets or maps) and avoids console warnings that can indirectly affect CWV scoring. Cloudflare’s own Pages documentation was refreshed in September 2024 to push these exact headers.

**Confidence**: high on the Chrome 130 release date and CSP recommendations; medium on exact “last 30 days” refresh timing of Cloudflare’s template (verify against Cloudflare blog).

### 3. Google AI Overviews citation refinements (ongoing iteration, significant update window mid-Sep to early Oct 2024)

- Strong schema.org markup (especially `FAQPage`, `HowTo`, `LocalBusiness` with `priceRange`, `openingHoursSpecification`, and `hasMap`).

- High INP and low CLS (Google’s systems appear to penalise jittery pages even when used as citations).

**Action**: Add or validate schema with Google’s Rich Results Test and ensure CLS < 0.1. Cloudflare Pages’ automatic minification + image optimisation helps here, but you may need explicit `fetchpriority="high"` on hero images.

**Confidence**: medium — the exact internal weighting change is not publicly dated to a single day, but public statements and SEO testing data cluster in the Sep/Oct window. Verify against Google’s Search Central AI Overviews documentation and Barry Schwartz / Glenn Gabe coverage.

perplexity.text:
The last 30 days have brought **no confirmed, documented changes to the official Core Web Vitals thresholds or Google’s page‑experience ranking signal**, but there *have* been meaningful shifts in **schema.org**, **Google AI Overviews for local business**, and the *practical* importance of existing CWV targets and AI search for small sites. Based on the sources retrieved, these are the three most important changes for a small Australian local‑business static site on Cloudflare Pages:

---

## 1. Schema.org 30.1 release (2026‑09‑16)

**What changed**

- **Schema.org Version 30.1** was published on **2026‑09‑16**.[2][5]  
- The release explicitly adds **new vocabulary to support discovery of EU Digital Product Passports** and other product‑related metadata.[2][5]  
  - This includes new/extended types and properties around product identity, traceability, and regulatory information (details are in the 30.1 release notes and diff).[2]

**Why it matters for a small AU local-business static site**

Even though EU Digital Product Passports are EU‑focused, the update signals:

- **Product‑rich results & compliance signals are expanding.** For any local business that sells physical products (e.g., bikes, electronics, appliances), structured data for product provenance and regulatory attributes is becoming more standard. Search engines often adopt and reward richer product markup with better product displays and potentially trust signals.[2]
- **Future‑proofing product schema:**  
  - If your local business site lists products (even in AU), aligning with the latest **schema.org 30.1** vocabulary makes it easier for Google and other AI systems to understand product details, origin, and compliance.  
  - That can affect visibility in rich results and AI summaries, especially as AI search experiences lean more on structured data.

**Concrete actions for your Cloudflare Pages site**

- Audit your current **Product**, **LocalBusiness**, and **Offer** markup against **schema.org 30.1**.[2][5]  
- Where relevant, start adding:
  - More detailed **product identifiers** (GTIN, SKU, model).
  - **Regulatory/compliance‑related properties** if applicable (e.g., energy ratings, eco‑labels, sustainability attributes).
- Keep using **JSON‑LD** embedded in your static pages, as that remains best practice for Google’s parsing of schema.org for local and product listings.

---

## 2. Google AI Overviews shifting local listings into AI summaries (mid‑September 2026)

**What changed**

- As of mid‑September 2026, Google has begun **turning local knowledge panels / Google Business Profiles into “AI Overview” listings**.[4]  
- Local search results can now show:
  - An **“AI Overview” label** at the top of the local listing.[4]  
  - A **“Show more” button** that opens a **chat‑style interface** (AI Mode) for follow‑up questions directly inside search.[4]  
- Separate reporting on Google AI Overviews for local businesses explains that these **AI‑generated summaries answer queries directly by combining information from several sites and then linking sources**.[7][15]  
- Recent commentary from Google/local‑search experts indicates Google’s AI can now **compare options, make decisions, and even book appointments without sending users to your website**.[13]

**Why it matters for your AU local-business static site**

For a local static site whose main discovery channel is Google Search:

- **Your website is increasingly a data source, not the primary destination.**
  - AI Overviews may summarize your business using:
    - Your **Google Business Profile** (GBP).
    - Structured data from your site.
    - Third‑party listings (review sites, directories).[4][7][15]
- **Click‑through from AI summaries may drop.**
  - Users can get opening hours, services, pricing ranges, and reviews from the AI Overview itself and even complete **booking or calling actions directly from Google’s interface**.[13]
- **Citation and inclusion depend on clarity and consistency of your business data.**
  - AI Overviews favor entities with:
    - Strongly consistent **NAP** (Name, Address, Phone) data.
    - Clear **service scope** and location.
    - Machine‑readable **schema.org LocalBusiness + openingHours + serviceArea** data.[7][13][15]

**Concrete actions for your Cloudflare Pages site**

On‑site:

- Ensure you have **complete, error‑free LocalBusiness schema**:
  - `name`, `address`, `telephone`, `openingHoursSpecification`, `geo`, `url`.
  - `sameAs` links (official social profiles, major directories).
- Make key business data **prominent in HTML** (not only in schema):
  - Plain‑text name, address, phone, and services on each relevant page.
- Implement **FAQPage schema** for common local queries (e.g., parking, payment methods, service area, accessibility) so AI Overviews can draw precise Q&A snippets.

Off‑site:

- Keep **Google Business Profile** fully up‑to‑date:
  - Categories, attributes (e.g., “Wheelchair accessible entrance”), booking links.
- Maintain **consistent NAP** across local directories (Bing Places, Apple Maps, Yelp, AU‑specific directories).
- Encourage **recent, high‑quality reviews**; AI systems heavily use review sentiment in summaries.[7][13]

---

## 3. Core Web Vitals: thresholds unchanged, but INP and CLS penalties clarified (ongoing into Sept 2026)

**What changed & what did *not* change**

From multiple sources updated mid‑September 2026:

- The **official, documented Core Web Vitals thresholds remain**:  
  - **LCP:** good ≤ **2.5 s**, needs improvement 2.5–4.0 s, poor > 4.0 s.[1][3][11][12][14]  
  - **INP:** good ≤ **200 ms**, needs improvement 200–500 ms, poor > 500 ms.[1][3][11][12][14]  
  - **CLS:** good ≤ **0.1**, needs improvement 0.1–0.25, poor > 0.25.[1][3][11][12][14]  
- These are assessed at the **75th percentile of real‑user (field) data**, separately for mobile and desktop, over a ~28‑day window.[1][3][11][12]
- Google’s own docs and several 2026 summaries confirm:
  - **INP fully replaced FID** as the responsiveness metric.[1][3][11][14]
  - Core Web Vitals remain a **page‑experience signal**, more of a **ranking tie‑breaker than a strong lever**.[1][3]
- Some commentary and hosting/SEO blogs in 2026 claim:
  - Tightened **desktop LCP “good” threshold to 2.0s** and increased **manual scrutiny for high mobile CLS** (especially >0.25 on heavily viewed pages).[8]  
  - More aggressive demotions for **INP > 500 ms**.[8]  
- However, these tighter numbers are not reflected in the **baseline thresholds** cited by more authoritative, doc‑aligned summaries.[1][3][11][12][14]

Given the mix of sources, the safest interpretation is:
